name: Mesha
overview: Mesha is a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Chelubai, also known as Caleb. His lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 2:42, situating him within the genealogical records of Judah. There are no additional notes or distinguishing details beyond his paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Mesha' appears as a proper name in Scripture without an associated meaning or divine origin indicated. It is simply recorded as the personal name of this individual in 1 Chronicles 2:42.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mesha as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and also mentions Ziph as his father, suggesting a close familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mesha's significance lies primarily in his placement within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Judah. His mention in 1 Chronicles 2:42 connects him to the lineage of Caleb, a notable figure, thereby preserving the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people. Although no specific deeds or roles are attributed to him, his inclusion underscores the importance of genealogies in understanding God's providential work through generations.
